takeaway: The SA node lies at the junction of the SVC and right atrium at the upper end of the sulcus terminalis, not medial to it.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the right atrium is false?

answer.text: Has the sinoatrial (SA) node medial to the sulcus terminalis
answer.say: Has the S A node medial to the sulcus terminalis

lines.text: Let us check the right atrium. The right atrium forms the right heart border, so that statement is true.
The coronary sinus opens into it, between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid valve.
Now the sinoatrial node. It lies near the opening of the superior vena cava, at the top of the sulcus terminalis.
It sits at the sulcus terminalis, it is not medial to it.
The interatrial septum forms the back wall, and the right atrium lies in front of the left atrium. Both are true.
So the false statement is: the SA node is medial to the sulcus terminalis.
